_comment: Values and phrases that must NOT appear as a current claim, with what
replaced them. scripts/make_tables.py --check fails on any of these in a
current document unless the line is marked <!-- historical -->, which is
how a retraction narrative quotes the number it is retracting.
WHY A LIST AND NOT A DERIVATION. The provenance checker asks whether a
token appears in SOME artifact. With 56 result sets and 101 archived
manifests, nearly every three-decimal number does -- so 0.945 was quoted
as the current HI-Large lift on five lines while the canonical lineage
says 0.9497, and the gate stayed green because 0.945 existed somewhere.
Token membership cannot express 'this number is the OLD answer'. Nothing
derives that. It has to be written down.

retracted.pattern: most of the separability|largely \*?\*?linear|separability is linear|there for the taking
retracted.was: an unmeasured share of the benchmark's separability attributed to linearity
retracted.now: logistic precision@50 = 0.57060 against an eight-seed GBDT mean of 0.82480 (range 0.59144-0.89815)
retracted.why: one baseline and one comparator cannot apportion separability; the fraction has no measured denominator, no ceiling and no preregistered estimand

retracted.pattern: benchmark gave away|what the benchmark gave
retracted.was: the same inference in shorthand
retracted.now: (nothing)
retracted.why: same defect: it asserts a share of the separability belongs to the generator without measuring one

retracted.pattern: substantially a property of (the benchmark|IBM|the simulator|the generator)|property of IBM's simulator|mostly a property of
retracted.was: an unmeasured share of a result attributed to the data generator
retracted.now: logistic precision@50 = 0.57060 against an eight-seed GBDT mean of 0.82480; the difference averages 0.254 and spans 0.021-0.328
retracted.why: the same attribution the 'most of the separability' retraction withdrew, in different words. No denominator, no ceiling, no attribution design

retracted.pattern: increment from model complexity is small|model complexity adds (only )?a small|gap the model adds is small
retracted.was: a judgement that the model's contribution is small
retracted.now: the GBDT-minus-logistic difference: mean 0.254, range 0.021-0.328 across eight seeds
retracted.why: 'small' is a judgement about a quantity with no stated scale, over a range that spans more than an order of magnitude

retracted.was: the alert-unit coupling restated in transaction units
retracted.now: at least 28 and at most 50 -- a bound, not a point value
retracted.why: the score-tie proxy CAN merge transactions -- unrelated transactions may share a score -- so the group count is a LOWER bound on distinct transactions and the ratio an UPPER bound on the over-counting factor, not an estimate. The 46.4% figure once cited as evidence for this was itself wrong and is separately retracted

retracted.was: an event-unit recall ceiling derived from the score-tie proxy
retracted.now: (nothing)
retracted.why: the factor was measured on the ALERTED set and applied to the positive POPULATION, and rests on a proxy that merges transactions. The field is no longer emitted

retracted.was: the event-unit ceiling on HI-Medium and its sensitivity range
retracted.now: (nothing)
retracted.why: same defect; an event-unit ceiling needs transaction identity for every account-day, which the archived bundles do not carry

retracted.was: the share of score groups said to span more than one ring transaction
retracted.now: 0% on all nine bundles, once the score source is required
retracted.why: the figures came from joining ring_endpoints to alerted account-days on (day, acct) with no score filter, which attaches an account-day to EVERY ring transaction touching the account rather than to the one that supplied its maximum. They measured 'this account-day touches several ring transactions', not score-group merging

retracted.was: account-days per ring transaction, called exact
retracted.why: same unfiltered join; the transaction count was inflated by transactions that did not cause the alert, which depressed the ratio

retracted.pattern: linear baseline is already strong|a linear model is already strong|linear model is already strong here
retracted.was: the headline reading of precision@50 = 0.5706, this file's self-declared biggest finding
retracted.now: retracted -- 97.0% of it comes from 12 days holding 0.056% of transactions; on volume days it is 0.0429 vs the GBDT's 0.7571
retracted.why: AMLworld's generator winds down (3,021,866 txns at 0.0008 prevalence on 09-16 -> 2,020 at 0.5936 on 09-17). The published window pools two regimes and `sum_d min(P_d,B)` inverts the intuition, so the tail is 59.2% of the ceiling despite holding 18.7% of positives

retracted.pattern: dominated by week one|dominated by the first week
retracted.was: the claim that budget metrics and the permutation null are driven by the busy days
retracted.now: the reverse: week one is 40.8% of the ceiling and 3.0% of the logistic model's true positives
retracted.why: reasoned from the 81.3% positive front-loading without noticing that the budget cap redistributes the attainable count toward the thin days

retracted.pattern: budget-binds framing survives|budget binds and that `ring_recall`
retracted.was: the claim that the budget-binds framing survives the window decomposition
retracted.now: false on the three days where the budget exceeds the population
retracted.why: 2022-09-26, 2022-09-27 and 2022-09-28 hold 44, 16 and 4 account-days against a budget of 50, so the top-50 is the whole day and precision@50 equals the day's prevalence for every ranker

retracted.was: the pooled logistic precision@50 quoted as a model-quality statement
retracted.now: 1.16x-1.26x a random ranker pooled; 10.18x on the volume segment
retracted.why: a uniformly random ranker scores 0.45392-0.49147 on the EVALUATED ring-aware test split because account-day prevalence runs 0.001926 to 1.0. The pooled level barely clears it and is not a model comparison. An earlier version of this entry said 0.60209 and 'below chance': that null was read from the raw CSV with only a date cut, so it included the 736 rings the split drops
retracted.scoping_note: line-scoped: the caveat may precede the number, so a forward-only lookahead missed correctly caveated lines

retracted.was: the typology-spread p-value
retracted.now: withdrawn. Against the repository's own within-day permutation null the observed spread of 3.46875 sits at the 53.5th percentile of chance (p = 0.46633), and the per-typology ordering INVERTS: GATHER-SCATTER 0.9159, CYCLE 1.264, rho(rate, lift) = 0.3095
retracted.why: a binomial H0 cannot describe a budget-constrained metric. 14 of the 529 evaluated rings end on a day where the budget exceeds the whole population and are caught by every ranker including a constant one -- and all 14 are GATHER-SCATTER, the numerator of the spread. The repo has documented that defect for precision@k since the section-1 retraction and never applied it to ring_recall
retracted.scoping_note: scoped to the `p = ` form: a bare 0.0008 also matches the wind-down prevalence, which is a different quantity entirely

retracted.was: the random-ranker null for precision@50 on HI-Medium
retracted.now: 0.45392-0.49147 on the evaluated ring-aware split
retracted.why: computed from the raw CSV with only a date cut, so it included the 736 dropped test rings -- 30,867 positive account-days against the evaluated 18,130. A 70% inflation of the positive class inflates a prevalence-weighted null

retracted.was: the volume-segment lifts over the null
retracted.now: 17.6x (logistic) and 310.3x (GBDT seed 0)
retracted.why: derived from the wrong-population null; the head null was 0.00421 and is 0.00243-0.00244 on the evaluated split

retracted.pattern: headline is below chance|below a uniformly random ranker|is \*\*below chance\*\*
retracted.was: the claim that the published precision@50 is below chance
retracted.now: it is ABOVE chance, by 1.16x-1.26x pooled
retracted.why: same wrong-population null. The direction of this conclusion reversed

retracted.was: the FIRST cliff-aware replacement for the typology-spread p-value: exposure 0.1925 (BIPARTITE) to 0.5863 (GATHER-SCATTER), rho 0.762 against detection, and p = 0.11-0.44 from assumed thin-day rates of 0.80/0.90/0.95
retracted.now: withdrawn. Against the repository's own within-day permutation null the observed spread of 3.46875 sits at the 53.5th percentile of chance (p = 0.46633), and the per-typology ordering INVERTS: GATHER-SCATTER 0.9159, CYCLE 1.264, rho(rate, lift) = 0.3095
retracted.why: two independent defects. (1) WRONG POPULATION: exposure was measured over every ring in the patterns file, including the 736 the ring-aware split drops, so it described a different ring set from the detection rates it was explaining. (2) INFEASIBLE ASSUMED RATES: an after-cliff share of 0.66352 and a pooled rate of 0.3724 cap the after-cliff rate at 0.56125, so 0.80/0.90/0.95 cannot reproduce the observed pooled rate at any head rate in [0,1]. Inside the feasible range the p-value spans 0.0014 to 0.9014, so the assumption chose the answer. Superseded entirely: the defensible null is the within-day permutation, not any binomial
retracted.scoping_note: `cliff_aware_spread` is registered as a bare key name because the withdrawn artifact field is the most likely route back in; `p = 0.17` is scoped to the p-value form so HI-Small's 0.170 is not matched

retracted.was: the SECOND cliff-aware replacement: exposure-only p = 0.0026 from fixed head/tail strata measured at ring budget 200 (tail 0.78348, head 0.57303, observed spread 1.85128, exposure-blind 1.2577), with rho 0.7143 and a t-approximated p = 0.0465
retracted.now: withdrawn. Against the repository's own within-day permutation null the observed spread of 3.46875 sits at the 53.5th percentile of chance (p = 0.46633), and the per-typology ordering INVERTS: GATHER-SCATTER 0.9159, CYCLE 1.264, rho(rate, lift) = 0.3095; exposure still correlates with the RAW rate at rho = 0.7857, exact permutation p = 0.02793, but that is a statement about the generator, not a detection result
retracted.why: three defects at once. (1) WRONG BUDGET: the 3.05x spread is ring_recall@50 -- src/aml/eval/metrics.py sets b = 50 -- while these strata were measured at 200, so the artifact published a tail rate of 0.78348 beside its own feasibility cap of 0.56125. (2) WRONG MODEL: medium_gbdt_s0 is source_lineage 'models'; its ring_recall@200 of 0.71267 matches none of the eight typology seeds. (3) WRONG NULL: two strata flatten a per-day process, and no binomial belongs on a budget-constrained metric. The rho was also a t-approximation on n=8; exactly, it is 0.0576, not 0.0465
retracted.scoping_note: scoped to the p-value and rate forms. 1.2577 and 1.85128 are registered bare because they appear nowhere else

retracted.was: the per-structure spread stated as an established finding, in WORDS
retracted.now: withdrawn: its H0 -- one detection probability per ring -- is false. No valid null has been computed for the 3.05x ensemble figure itself; on the nearest measurable basis (one archived replay, current ring join, ring_recall@50) the observed spread is the 53.5th percentile of chance (p = 0.46633) and no per-typology ordering is established
retracted.why: the registry matched the withdrawn NUMBER and nothing else, so the claim walked back in as prose: paper/README.md indexed this result as 'significant on HI-Medium' while the file it linked to retracted it, and no gate could see the contradiction. Register the CLAIM, not only its digits
retracted.scoping_note: prose forms only; the numeric forms are registered above

retracted.was: three withdrawn claims restated without their digits: the 1.43 ring-recall lift, 'near-saturated', and '97% of the uplift is prevalence'
retracted.now: lift 0.9497 against a within-day permutation null; 'saturated' is removed from every current document; the decomposition is 47% prevalence / 53% detectability
retracted.why: a probe of all 29 patterns found that every prose paraphrase and every numeric reformat passed clean -- '1.43 times chance', '143% of chance', 'nearly saturated', '97 percent prevalence'. A registry that matches only the exact string it was given catches the copy-paste and misses the rewrite
retracted.scoping_note: word forms; the digit forms are registered separately
